newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas surges on cold, low stocks.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas surges on cold, low stocks.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were sharply higher Friday, lifted by severely cold temperatures and eroding storage inventories in the West, sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, prices ranged anywhere from C$2.60 to C$2.90 per gigajoule (GJ) as temperatures were forecast to slip to -34 degrees C on Saturday.
Traders said most deals were done at AECO in the C$3.73-3.78 per GJ range, up about 40 cents from Thursday.
Canadian Gas Association said gas inventories as of January 17 were at 102.11 bcf in the West, or 39.41 percent of capacity. These data compare with 52.41 percent full a year ago.
Traders have estimated that about 1.2-1.3 bcf of gas is being withdrawn from storage on a daily basis during this cold snap.
"Gas is flying out of storage, and we still have a lot of winter to go," one Calgary-based trader said.
At Sumas, Wash., prices rose by about 20 cents to the $2.80-2.95 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) range, boosted by maintenance on Westcoast's system and cold temperatures in western Canada.

Westcoast said interruptible transportation would be reduced on Monday by about 10 percent to 650 million cubic feet per day from 730 mmcfd to perform an acid wash at its McMahon gas plant in British Columbia.
Traders have also noted that maintenance at its Fort Nelson plant will reduce gas flows to about 43 percent Saturday.
Westcoast was not immediately available for comment on the Fort Nelson maintenance.
Further east, where temperatures are not as severe and storage inventories are ahead of year-ago levels, Niagara prices edged up about five to six cents to the $3.10-3.15 per mmBtu range.
CGA said stocks in the East were at 123.95 bcf, or 53.3 percent full, as compared with 52.41 percent full a year ago.
